tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description opens with imperative phrasing ('Use this skill to assess...', 'Use it when...'), lists many explicit trigger contexts (outdated databases, EOL, Extended Support, past failed upgrades, downtime strategy, periodic audits), focuses on user intent (what the user is asking) rather than internals, and is a concise paragraph.
tests.evidence: Use this skill to assess Amazon RDS and Aurora databases for major-version upgrade readiness across engines... Use it when a user asks which databases are outdated, end-of-life, approaching end of support, or on RDS Extended Support; why a past upgrade failed...

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense but every sentence conveys domain-specific, non-obvious information (engine dispatch rules, calendar classification thresholds, AWS API calls, engine-specific caveats). It does not explain generic concepts like what RDS or an upgrade is.
tests.evidence: Aurora and RDS of the same community version can have DIFFERENT dates, so always use the correct engine section of the calendar.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed per-engine data (EOL dates, findings classification tables, dispatch tables) is placed in references/ files and only linked/summarized in the body. The body retains only short per-engine caveat bullets, which are concise decision points, not full tables.
tests.evidence: Open the engine's calendar file (identified in Step 3). Read the engine's EOL calendar when classifying that engine's version — load [mysql/Aurora MySQL](references/mysql-eol-calendar.md)...

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file in references/ has at least one markdown link in the body using the references/<filename> pattern.
tests.evidence: [engine dispatch reference](references/engine-dispatch.md), [mysql/Aurora MySQL](references/mysql-eol-calendar.md), [PostgreSQL](references/postgresql-eol-calendar.md), [MariaDB](references/mariadb-eol-calendar.md), [Oracle](references/oracle-eol-calendar.md), [SQL Server](references/sqlserver-eol-calendar.md), [Db2](references/db2-eol-calendar.md), [MySQL / Aurora MySQL findings](references/precheck-findings-reference.md), [PostgreSQL findings](references/postgresql-precheck-findings-reference.md), [MariaDB findings](references/mariadb-precheck-findings-reference.md), [SQL Server / Oracle review](references/sqlserver-oracle-review-reference.md), [Db2 findings](references/db2-upgrade-findings-reference.md)

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is paired with a specific trigger condition describing when to load it (e.g., when detecting Engine, when classifying a version, when parsing evidence for a specific engine).
tests.evidence: Read [engine dispatch reference](references/engine-dispatch.md) when you first detect a database's `Engine`, to pick its calendar, past-upgrade artifact, findings reference, and version-major parsing rule.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/ with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile, consistency-critical operations (version classification thresholds, read-only guardrails, engine dispatch) are given exact rules, while flexible analysis tasks (ranking upgrade methods, remediation ordering) are explained with rationale allowing judgment.
tests.evidence: Blue/Green — lowest downtime (~5s switchover); replicates Multi-AZ automatically. Rank #1 for production, Multi-AZ, or clustered/Aurora.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: When presenting upgrade strategy options, the skill explicitly ranks them with a clear default (Blue/Green) and alternatives as fallbacks for specific cases.
tests.evidence: Rank #1 for production, Multi-AZ, or clustered/Aurora... In-place — simplest... Rank #1 only for non-prod single-AZ.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable multi-phase procedure (discover, classify, analyze evidence, recommend strategy) applicable to any database/account, not a one-off instance task.
tests.evidence: Phase 1 — Discover databases, config view, and version/EOL status... Phase 2 — Analyze past failed/blocked upgrade evidence... Phase 3 — Recommend an upgrade strategy

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an explicit empirical gotcha section documenting a non-obvious divergence between RDS and Aurora MySQL precheck behavior, plus numerous engine-specific caveats throughout Phase 3.
tests.evidence: Cross-engine precheck divergence (EMPIRICAL — MySQL only, so far)... Treat such an Aurora WARNING as HIGH-PRIORITY action-required.
